brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Hex base unit: full bases piece:-1,0,0, piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0 on level 0, with full base piece:0,0,1 and piece:-1,0,1 stacked on level 1 as shelves, plus snaps joining them. check_build reports meshClash clear.
Two drawers drawer:0#0,-1#cut and drawer:0#1,-1#cut, one on each cut face of the half bases piece:0,-1,0 (half-n) and piece:1,-1,0 (half-n).

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; it has no load rating or material strength data. The load capacity depends on the printed material and infill, which I cannot verify. No load rating is claimed.

lockJoints added joint bolts at piece:0,0,0 and piece:1,0,0 so the bases cannot slide apart. capOpenFaces was refused with MESH_CLASH against the drawer frame (5 mm), so the open faces remain uncapped; the build is otherwise clear.

finish.summary: Built a small hex-base shelf unit: three full bases on the ground level, two half bases with a drawer each on the front, and two shelf bases above. Joints are bolted and the mesh check is clear. The 50 kg book rating cannot be verified by the configurator, and load depends on the material you print in, so that requirement is unmet. Open faces could not be capped because the cap would clash with the drawer frames.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
